sections.h2: Where does a Knox County seller record a deed?
sections.html:
The recorder in Mount Vernon files Knox County deeds, but the auditor sees them first. The auditor's office is at 117 East High Street, Suite 120, Mount Vernon, OH 43050. Its published weekday hours are 8:00 to 4:00, the real estate desk answers at 740-393-6745, and the exemption desk at 740-393-6748. Phone the recorder's office for its own counter hours, payment methods and mailing rules before a deed goes in the mail.

Ohio gives each county a single recorder. Whether the house sits in town, near Fredericktown or around Gambier, the paperwork follows the same route through that one Mount Vernon office.

sections.h2: What does the Knox County auditor charge when a deed transfers?
sections.html:
The auditor's home page says Knox County's conveyance fee is $3.00 per thousand dollars of the sale price. Section 319.54(G)(2) adds fifty cents per transfer or entry. After the auditor, the recorder bills under section 317.32, where each charge pairs a base fee with a housing trust fund fee.

What a Knox County deed can cost, from the auditor's home page and Ohio Revised Code sections 317.32, 317.114 and 319.54
ChargePrinted amount
Conveyance fee (auditor)$3.00 per thousand dollars of the sale price
Transfer or entry (auditor)$0.50 each
Recording a two page deed$17 base fee, matched by a $17 housing trust fund fee
Every page past two$4 base fee, matched by a $4 housing trust fund fee
Preservation surchargeUp to $5, a county option
Marginal reference$2 plus $2 for each reference
Deed that ignores the layout rules$10 plus $10 on top of the usual charge

Ask the recorder whether the surcharge applies and what your page count totals.

sections.h2: Who files the statement of value, and who pays?
sections.html:
The buyer files it, and the seller pays, under section 319.202. The figure reported is the full price, mortgage included, and a false number is a violation. A county transfer tax, if one is levied, is collected the same way before the deed moves on to the recorder.

Knox County's auditor posts these forms for a sale:

  • DTE 100 records the statement of value and doubles as the receipt.
  • DTE 100(EX) names the reason a deed owes nothing.
  • DTE 101 discloses a conveyance of homestead property.
  • DTE 102 covers land enrolled in the current agricultural use valuation, common on farm acreage here.

The statute asks the buyer to affirm that the seller was questioned about any homestead reduction and any farm valuation. Tell the closing agent about either one early.

sections.h2: Which Knox County deeds owe no conveyance fee?
sections.html:
The exemption list in section 319.54(G)(3) is long. The entries a homeowner is likeliest to use:

  • Gifts between spouses, or from a parent to a child.
  • Transfers among a decedent's heirs when no money changes hands.
  • Deeds into a trust the maker can revoke, and deeds back out of it.
  • Corrective deeds that repair an earlier recorded one.
  • Interests worth $100 or less.

Government, charity and court-ordered transfers appear on the list too. An exempt deed still needs the exemption form, so ask the real estate desk which form fits.

sections.h2: How must a deed be laid out for the Knox County recorder?
sections.html: Section 317.114 asks for ten point type or larger, paper between letter and legal size, dark ink, no highlighter, one inch margins on the sides and bottom, and a three inch clear band across the top of page one. The recorder will still take a deed that misses these, at the added cost shown in the table. Court filings, plats, agency papers and instruments signed before July 1, 2009 are outside the rule.

sections.h2: What is Knox County like beyond the courthouse?
sections.html:
Knox County split off from Fairfield County in 1808 and carries the name of Henry Knox. It spans 525.50 square miles of land at about 119 people per square mile, with rolling hills in the glaciated Allegheny Plateau. Wikipedia puts farmland near 58 percent of the county and forest near 28 percent, and Mount Vernon is the single city.

Census QuickFacts counts 64,002 people in mid 2025, a gain of 2.0 percent since April 2020, in 26,668 housing units. Three out of four homes are owner occupied (75.5 percent). Home values: $239,400 median for 2020 to 2024. Rent: $950 median gross. Households: 23,491, at a median income of $73,878. Eighty nine percent of households have broadband (89.3 percent), 91.0 percent of adults finished high school and 24.7 percent hold a bachelor's degree. About 89.8 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, and 270 building permits were issued in 2025.

The local payroll includes Siemens Energy and Ariel Corporation in Mount Vernon, Kenyon College in Gambier, Mount Vernon Nazarene University and Kokosing Construction near Fredericktown, and agriculture is large, with corn the main crop.

sections.h2: What can a Knox County owner check on the auditor's site before listing?
sections.html:
The auditor runs a real estate search portal that was upgraded for use on phones and tablets, plus a tax estimator, a GIS and tax map page and a downloadable property data correction form. If a deed splits acreage, the forms page carries a split form and a form for the proposed division of valuation on split acreage, which matters for owners selling off a lot from a larger farm parcel.

  • Run the parcel search and compare the owner name and acreage with your deed.
  • Try the tax estimator for a rough tax figure to show a buyer.
  • Download the property data correction form if a record shows the wrong square footage or building count.
  • Read the sheriff sales page if the parcel has a case in court.

The auditor's home page adds that the office does not give out phone numbers for property owners, so buyers and agents should contact you through the listing.

sections.h2: When are Knox County real estate taxes due, and where do disputes go?
sections.html:
For 2026 the auditor's page lists February 13 and August 26, and both dates are past. Ask the Knox County Treasurer for the next pair. The auditor links to the treasurer's payment site from its home page.

Value complaints go to the Knox County Board of Revision. The auditor's notice says the board organizes on January 4, 2027 and takes formal complaints from January 1 through March 31, 2027, and that the 2026 returns can be inspected at the auditor's office. The auditor's menu also links pages for the owner occupancy reduction, homestead exemption, CAUV soil rates, agricultural districts and sheriff sales.

When a tax bill is still open at closing, the title company typically gets a payoff from the treasurer and settles it from the proceeds. Request that figure as soon as a contract exists.

faqs.q: Who records a deed in Knox County, Ohio?
faqs.a: The Knox County Recorder in Mount Vernon. The deed visits the auditor at 117 East High Street, Suite 120 beforehand. Call the recorder for current hours and mailing instructions.

faqs.q: What is the Knox County conveyance fee?
faqs.a: The auditor's home page states $3.00 per thousand dollars of the sale price, and section 319.54(G)(2) adds fifty cents per transfer or entry. Under section 319.202 the seller bears it.

faqs.q: What if my deed ignores the margin and ink rules?
faqs.a: The recorder takes it anyway and collects an extra $10 base fee and $10 housing trust fund fee. Court papers, plats, agency documents and instruments from before July 1, 2009 are excluded.

faqs.q: Can I give a Knox County house to my child without the conveyance fee?
faqs.a: A gift from a parent to a child is on the exemption list in section 319.54(G)(3). File the DTE 100(EX) with the auditor. The recorder's own charges still apply.

faqs.q: Which forms apply to farm ground or a homestead parcel in Knox County?
faqs.a: The auditor lists DTE 101 for homestead property and DTE 102 for current agricultural use valuation property. Ask the auditor about any recoupment charge on farm land before closing.
